messages:
rachel: quick follow-up after the pinning rfc review: can we define explicit "schema gates" instead of implicit field-by-field compat? low-cost to check and clearer rollouts.
marta: sounds useful. what's a schema gate in this context?
rachel: gate = (meta_version, capabilities_set) pair. servers publish max_supported gate in control-plane. clients advertise desired gate via header. negotiation maps to lowest common gate.
jin: that seems similar to version headers but more expressive. how does it help day-to-day?
rachel: a couple of wins: 1) single checkpoint to accept/reject new semantics, 2) easier telemetry for skew, 3) simpler opt-in strict mode.
owen: does this force clients to include the whole pin object? we still want compact representations for bandwidth sensitive SDKs.
rachel: yes we separate concerns: gate decides semantics; encoding still allowed to be compact (compact anchor tokens / delta pins) as long as the gate signals decoder support.
marta: edge-case: if client sends compact token but server knows gate < compact-v1, server must expand or reject?
rachel: preference: expand if control-plane has mapping from compact -> canonical. if mapping missing: treat as advisory and normalize to best-effort; emit meta_skew telemetry. Add opt-in strict header to force rejections in canaries.
jin: security question: signed vs unsigned encodings. compact tokens could be forged. must require server-side verification for any routing/significant semantics.
kevin: suggest short HMAC prefix + kid in token (keeps size small) and require servers to verify for any gate that enables signed semantics. unsigned tokens only provide hints.
marta: agreed. and document which fields are authoritative (tenant_id, hard_ttl, origin) and which are hints (soft_ttl, affinity, rollout_hint).
owen: rollout path: 1) add `X-RW-SCHEMA-GATE: name:v` header, 2) servers report `X-RW-GATE-RES` header (`ok|normalized|rejected`), 3) control-plane exposes `max_gate` per region.
ops-bot: NOTE: add runbook entry - if unexpected rejects spike set `X-RW-META-STRICT: 1` on control-plane to force immediate breakage detection.
jin: SDKs: default to legacy gate until we flip a feature flag. Add a local `rw-gate-decode` cli to inspect gate->schema mapping.
rachel: telemetry fields: `client_gate`, `server_gate`, `gate_skew_bool`, `gate_reject_code` with values (unsupported, malformed, auth_fail), and `bytes_saved_compact` histogram.
kevin: implementation detail: gate strings should be compact ascii tokens (no long names) e.g., `g1`, `g2:compact`, `g3:signed`. Keep registry small.
marta: testing: generate randomized gate permutations and assert servers either normalize or reject with code. Also e2e with canary region where control-plane max_gate = g1 while clients try g2.
rachel: migration notes: never change semantics of anchor fields across gates. Gates only add optional, backward-compatible hints. If a gate would change anchor semantics we must create a hard migration window with coordinated rollout and a strict opt-in.
owen: ops concern: how to roll back if signed tokens cause routing issues? we need key-rotation and emergency key-revoke path plus the opt-out header.
kevin: key revoke: control-plane publishes revoked_kids list; servers check and treat revoked as unsigned. Also we can set `X-RW-IGNORE-GATE-SIGNING: 1` at edge for emergency.
marta: action items: Rachel: draft gate registry and naming. Jin: HMAC prefix + key rotation doc. Owen: ops rollback + control-plane max_gate plan. Kevin: prototype `rw-gate-decode` and sample tokens. I'll own telemetry and dashboards.
rachel: I'll open the PR today with examples and a small diff of the compact token grammar. please leave comments. :thumbsup:
